base_year_label: mixed 2024-2026 nominal USD; no escalation index applied

equipment_shares_pct.source: Chopra et al. 2026 p. 5 Fig. 5(a) shares of TCI, compressor (44 %) removed and renormalised (derived)

pec_reference_kUSD.note: Cost year not stated. Unit kUSD inferred (consistent with yearly CAPEX in the text); see economics.yaml; citekey farokhi2025costoptimization.
pec_reference_kUSD.source: Farokhi, Oi & Hansen 2025 (IFAC-PapersOnLine 59, 48-53) p. 5 Table 5 (PEC at 500 kmol/h NH3 feed)

scaling_exponent.source: Chopra et al. 2026 p. 4 Eq. 5 (all equipment)

singapore_location_factor.source: No sourced Singapore location factor found; set to 1.0 (assumption). Chopra's India factor 0.65 is not transferable.

tci_over_pec.source: Farokhi 2025 p. 5 Table 5: TCI 10,096 kUSD / PEC 1,702 kUSD (derived); installation, indirect and working-capital items are inside this ratio

carbon_tax.note: Verified: 5 (2019-23), 25 (2024-25), 45 (2026 and any later emissions year under the Carbon Pricing Act 2018, Third Schedule; the key '2026-2027' above is kept for compatibility), 50-80 by 2030 'with a view to' (an aim, not legislated). Budget 2026 statements said the 2030 rate could be at the lower end of the range if global momentum weakens (search-result summary). N2O is a covered gas but no N2O emission factor for ammonia combustion is available from a primary source, so AmCraX does not quantify it (see singapore.py).
carbon_tax.scope: direct (Scope 1) facility-level emissions from fuel combustion and industrial processes; facilities >= 25,000 tCO2e/yr
carbon_tax.source: National Environment Agency, Carbon Tax page (also NCCS Carbon Tax page); the 2030 range is intended, not legislated (IETA brief, July 2025)

catalyst.note: Prices (Ni 33.4, Ru 542 USD/kg), lifetime (2 yr, assumed by the authors) and space velocity (9,000 mL NH3/(g h)): Cho et al. 2026 p. 7 Table 4 and p. 6 Table 3; see economics.yaml. Inventory sized from that space velocity by default.

fees_SGD_per_kWh.source: same SP Group page (MSS 0.23 + market admin/PSO 0.08 cents)

industrial_all_in_price.note: No official industrial all-in contract price was found. Base case = USEP 2025 mean + network + fees (derived, assumption that a large user pays wholesale energy plus network and fees). Electricity is below 0.1 % of LCOH in the baseline, so the choice is not material.

regulated_tariff_Q4_2026_SGD_per_kWh.note: Regulated (household/small consumer) tariff; NOT an industrial contract price. Used as the upper bound.
regulated_tariff_Q4_2026_SGD_per_kWh.source: SP Group tariff information, 1 Oct-31 Dec 2026: energy 22.18 + network 6.10 + MSS 0.23 + market admin/PSO 0.08 = 28.59 cents/kWh

usep_2025_monthly_SGD_per_MWh.note: Energy price only (wholesale). Unweighted mean of the 12 monthly values is computed in code (116.6 SGD/MWh); not an official annual figure.
usep_2025_monthly_SGD_per_MWh.source: EMA Average Monthly USEP table (monthly values as relayed by a search result; 2026 months Jan-Aug rose from 118.6 to 332.5 on fuel prices)

fx_SGD_per_USD.note: PHASE 2: SUPERSEDED. Code uses currency.fx_SGD_per_USD of data/reference_scenario.yaml (ECB cross rate 1.288444, 20 Nov 2026); this Phase 1 record is kept as a cross-check. Review check 2026-11-23: the cited ADB page itself shows 1.290 at 'Close of November 20, 2026' (same value). Official MAS/data.gov.sg daily rate could not be retrieved. Rate date originally recorded: 2026-11-18. Used only to convert SGD tariffs and the carbon tax. Commerzbank commentary (19 Nov 2026) expects 1.28-1.30.
fx_SGD_per_USD.source: Asian Bonds Online (ADB), Singapore economy page: SGD per USD close 18 Nov 2026 = 1.290 (search-result snippet; MAS series not retrieved)

natural_gas_co2_factor_kg_per_GJ.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines default natural gas 56.1 t CO2/TJ, as printed in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 Annex VI (search-result snippet)

singapore_natural_gas_price.note: No Singapore industrial gas price was retrieved (EMA statistics page returned no text). EMA June 2026 factsheet states imported natural gas is 95 % of electricity production. The gas-fired heat variant uses the Kum et al. 2026 fired-heat price (4.25 USD/GJ, p. 8 Table 5), international and labelled so.

blue_delivered_east_asia.source: ACE report estimate for delivered cost to East Asia: 5-7 USD/kg blue, 9-11 USD/kg green (search-result summary); 6.0 = midpoint (derived)

low_carbon_offer_fob_malaysia.source: S&P Global, indicative offers of low-carbon hydrogen at about 10 USD/kg FOB Malaysia, May 2025 (search-result summary)

ne_asia_smr_production_cost.note: Corrected by the independent review (docs/internal/research_review.md): the earlier value 4.68 ('7 Apr 2026 marker', search-result text) does not appear in the cited document. Production-cost marker, not a selling price.
ne_asia_smr_production_cost.source: Argus Hydrogen and Future Fuels, issue 26-01 (6 Jan 2026) sample report, p. 2 'Regional hydrogen cost markers 6 Jan': Northeast Asia baseline SMR, incl. capex 3.06 USD/kg (excl. capex 2.09); read from the PDF text of the cited URL

h2_price_benchmarks_USD_per_kg.note: Benchmarks differ in basis (production cost vs delivered vs offer price, FOB vs delivered) and are not directly comparable. Breaks-even results are reported per benchmark, none is a Singapore transaction price.

sg_low_carbon_willingness_to_pay.source: S&P Global, 'Power generation firms face high hydrogen costs in Singapore', 7 May 2025: willingness to pay for low-carbon hydrogen in Singapore about 3 USD/kg (search-result summary; article not fetched)

blue.note: Low and high are the two regional assessments; the base 487 is their arithmetic mean (derived). Far East Asia blue below the Cho grey base reflects the date and basis difference; kept visible, not adjusted.
blue.source: S&P Global Platts blue ammonia assessments, July 2025: Far East Asia 400 USD/mt, Northwest Europe 574 USD/mt (search-result snippet; article returned HTTP 403)

green_2030.source: Cho et al. 2026 p. 17 (709 USD/t sensitivity); Table 9 range 472-946 USD/t for 2030 (IRENA 2022)

green_2050.source: Cho et al. 2026 p. 17 (463 USD/t); Table 9 range 315-611 USD/t for 2050 (IRENA 2022)

green_current.source: Cho et al. 2026 p. 17 Fig. 11 (renewable NH3, current 1,000 USD/t; Table 9 cites IEA ETP 2023); range 887-1,052 USD/t = S&P Platts delivered green ammonia early 2025 (search-result snippet)

grey.note: Conventional (fossil, unabated) ammonia. International figure, not Singapore.
grey.source: Cho et al. 2026 Energy Convers. Manage. 348, 120796, p. 7 Table 4 (450, 'assumed'); conventional NH3 range 300-610 USD/t, Table 8

ammonia_power_bunkering_project.note: Direct combustion, not cracking; consistent with the Halim et al. 2025 conclusion. No claim that a cracker facility exists.
ammonia_power_bunkering_project.value: Keppel-led consortium appointed 3 Oct 2025 for FEED of a 55-65 MW direct-combustion ammonia power plant and at least 0.1 Mt/yr bunkering (EMA and MPA)

halim_2025.value: Halim, Zain & Khoo (2025) Appl. Energy 386, 125581: direct ammonia use preferred economically over cracking for power; green ammonia near-zero emissions; blue from SMR a transitional option. Full text read on 24 November 2026 (research/notes/halim2025_full_text.md): LCOH 15.1 (green) and 10.1 (blue) USD/kg H2 and the 60.1 MW plant are located (p. 3, p. 9, Fig. 5, Table 5); the paper's 'about 40 %' is a fuel cost at the turbine inlet (1 - LCOA/LCOH), not a cost of electricity. Context only; no AmCraX input is taken from it.

national_hydrogen_strategy.value: Launched October 2022; low-carbon hydrogen for power decarbonisation; at least four hydrogen-ready plants by 2030 (search-result summary of MTI/Norton Rose Fulbright)
